/* ============================================================================
CHART (the charts of dashboards: pie, donut, gauge, heatmap, sparkline)

One widget, five kinds (RChartKind), each fed by its own calls:

R_CHART_PIE, R_CHART_DONUT   slices: Rchart_add_slice and the others
R_CHART_GAUGE                Rchart_set_range, Rchart_set_value, bands
R_CHART_HEATMAP              Rchart_set_grid, labels of the rows and columns
R_CHART_SPARKLINE            Rchart_set_values or Rchart_push_value

The colors follow the theme: the slices take the accent then a palette
of ten colors made for the dark and the light themes, the gauge and the
sparkline the accent (Rchart_set_color), the heatmap goes from a tint of
the accent to the accent. The values glide to their new place when they
change. The pointer over a slice lifts it and tells its label, value and
share; over a cell of a heatmap or a point of a sparkline, its value. A
click on a slice selects it (and again, unselects it), a click on a cell
calls the cell callback; both also fire the action of the widget.
The background is left to what holds the chart (a tile, a panel).

Slices, bands, rows, columns and values are counted from 0.

XML:
<Chart Kind="Donut" Title="Browsers" Format="%.0f">
<Slice Label="Chrome" Value="64"/> <Slice Label="Safari" Value="19" Color="#ff9f0a"/>
</Chart>
<Chart Kind="Gauge" Min="0" Max="100" Value="72" Format="%.0f%%">
<Band From="0" To="60"/> <Band From="60" To="85"/> <Band From="85" To="100"/>
</Chart>
<Chart Kind="Heatmap" ColumnLabels="0|6|12|18"> <Row Label="Mon" Values="1 4 2 0"/> ... </Chart>
<Chart Kind="Sparkline" Values="3 5 4 6 8 7 9"/>
============================================================================ */

/** brief A chart of a kind (Rwidget_create(R_WIDGET_CHART) makes a pie).

Rchart_set_title.doc: The title over a pie, a donut or a heatmap, under the value of a gauge (a sparkline only tells it to screen readers).

Rchart_set_format.doc:
How the values are written (the gauge, the middle of a donut, what
the pointer shows): a printf format for one double with its unit, "%.0f%%",
"$%.2f". NULL: whole numbers as they are, others with up to two decimals.

Rchart_set_color.doc: The color of the arc of a gauge outside any band, and of the line of a sparkline (default: the accent).

Rchart_set_legend.doc: The legend: the slices beside a pie or a donut, the scale of colors under a heatmap (shown by default).

Rchart_clear.doc: Removes the slices, the bands, the grid and the values.

Rchart_get_hovered.doc:
What is under the pointer: a slice, a point of a sparkline, or a
cell of a heatmap as row * columns + column; -1 for nothing.

Rchart_add_slice.doc: Adds a slice (a value of 0 or more). Returns its index, -1 when the value is not valid.

Rchart_set_slice_color.doc: The color of a slice; an alpha of 0 gives it back its color of the palette.

Rchart_get_total.doc: The sum of the values of the slices.

Rchart_set_selected.doc: The slice lifted as selected, or -1 for none (the user selects one with a click).

Rchart_set_hole.doc: The hole of a donut, as a part of its radius, from 0.2 to 0.9 (default 0.62).

Rchart_set_center_text.doc:
What the middle of a donut shows when the pointer is not over a
slice: `text` in large (NULL or "": the total) over `caption` in small
(NULL or "": none).

Rchart_get_range.doc: The range in use now (a gauge's, or the one of the values of a heatmap or a sparkline).

Rchart_set_value.doc: The value of a gauge, kept within its range when drawn.

Rchart_add_band.doc:
Colors a part of the range of a gauge (an alpha of 0: the success,
warning and danger colors of the theme, one after the other). The arc
takes the color of the band its value is in. Returns the index of the band.

Rchart_set_grid.doc:
The cells of a heatmap: `rows` x `columns` values, row after row,
copied (NULL: all 0). NaN leaves a cell empty.

Rchart_set_row_labels.doc: The names of the rows, separated by '|': "Mon|Tue|Wed" (shown at their left).

Rchart_set_column_labels.doc: The names of the columns, separated by '|' (shown over them, as many as fit).

Rchart_get_row_label.doc: The name of a row or of a column, "" when it has none.

Rchart_set_color_scale.doc: The colors of the lowest and of the highest values of a heatmap (default: a tint of the accent, the accent).

Rchart_push_value.doc: Adds a value after the others, for live data; only the last `max_count` are kept (0: all of them).

Rchart_set_fill.doc: Shades the area under the line of a sparkline (on by default).

Rchart_set_marker.doc: A dot on the last value of a sparkline (on by default).

Rpdf_is_available.doc: R_TRUE when PDFium can be loaded (it is, the first time this is asked).

Rpdf_view_load_file.doc:
Shows a PDF file. `password` may be NULL. Returns R_FALSE when it
cannot: Rpdf_view_get_status tells why (a password is needed, not a
PDF, no PDFium). The view then shows that instead of pages.

Rpdf_view_load_memory.doc: Same as Rpdf_view_load_file, from bytes in memory (copied).

Rpdf_view_close.doc: Closes the document: the view is empty.

Rpdf_view_get_page_size.doc: Size of a page in points (1/72 inch), as it is shown (its rotation applied).

Rpdf_view_set_page.doc: Scrolls to the top of a page; it becomes the current page.

Rpdf_view_get_page.doc: The current page: the one a third down the view.

Rpdf_view_set_zoom.doc: A zoom of its own (1: the printed size): the fit becomes R_PDF_FIT_NONE.

Rpdf_view_get_zoom.doc: The zoom the pages show at, the one a fit gives included.

Rpdf_view_get_title.doc: The title of the document (its information), "" when it has none.

Rpdf_view_get_page_text.doc:
The text of a page (UTF-8), to search it or copy it. Valid until
the next call for this view.

Rpdf_document_set_title.doc: The information of the document, shown by readers (the title in their window).

Rpdf_document_add_page.doc: Adds a page of a size in points; drawing goes to it. Returns its index, -1 for an invalid size.

Rpdf_document_set_line_width.doc: Width of the lines and outlines, in points (default 1).

Rpdf_document_draw_rect.doc: A rectangle, its corners rounded by `radius`; `paint` is a bitmask of RPdfPaint.

Rpdf_document_draw_line.doc: A line in the stroke color.

Rpdf_document_add_font.doc:
Adds a TrueType font (.ttf) to the document (the data is
copied, and embedded in the file). Returns its number for
Rpdf_document_set_font, -1 when it is not a TrueType font.

Rpdf_document_set_font.doc: The font of the text drawn next: an RPdfFont or a number of Rpdf_document_add_font, a size in points, a bitmask of RPdfTextStyle.

Rpdf_document_get_line_height.doc: Distance between two lines of text in the current font.

Rpdf_document_measure_text.doc: Width of a text in the current font, in points (of its widest line).

Rpdf_document_draw_text.doc:
Text in the fill color, the top of its first line at y ('\n'
starts a line below). Returns its width.

Rpdf_document_draw_paragraph.doc:
Text wrapped at the spaces to fit `width`, each line placed by
`align` (R_HALIGN_LEFT, R_HALIGN_CENTER or R_HALIGN_RIGHT). Returns the
height it took.

Rpdf_document_draw_image.doc:
A picture of RGBA8 pixels stretched over a rectangle. A width or
height of 0 keeps the proportions of the picture; both 0: 96 pixels per inch.

Rpdf_document_draw_window.doc:
What a window shows (Rwindow_capture), as a picture: a report of
the screen, a chart. A width and height of 0: the size it has on the
screen. Returns R_FALSE when the window cannot be captured.

Rpdf_document_save.doc: Writes the file. Returns R_FALSE when it cannot be written.

Rpdf_document_save_memory.doc: The file in memory (followed by a '\0' not counted), to release with Rmemory_free; `size` receives its length.

Rpdf_print.doc:
Prints a PDF document with the print system: on macOS the print
panel, on Windows the print dialog (the pages are drawn by PDFium, see
PDF VIEW), on Linux and the other systems CUPS (lp or lpr) after a
dialog of Raven that chooses the printer. It waits until the job is
sent. `desc` may be NULL. Returns R_FALSE when cancelled or when it
cannot print. Not in the browser.

Rpdf_document_print.doc: Prints a document written by the application.

Rtext_editor_set_text.doc: Replaces the whole text. The history of undo is cleared; the changed callback is not called.

Rtext_editor_get_text.doc: Returns The whole text, lines separated by '\n'. Valid until the next call or the next edit.

Rtext_editor_get_length.doc: Returns The number of bytes of Rtext_editor_get_text.

Rtext_editor_get_line.doc: Returns One line, without its line break. Valid until the next edit. NULL when `line` is out of range.

Rtext_editor_insert_text.doc:
Types a text at the cursor, replacing the selection, as the user
would: it can be undone and the changed callback is called.

Rtext_editor_select.doc: Selects from one position to another; the cursor is on the second.

Rtext_editor_get_selection.doc: Start and end of the selection, in the order of the text. Returns R_FALSE when nothing is selected.

Rtext_editor_get_selected_text.doc: Returns The selected text, "" when there is none. Valid until the next call or the next edit.

Rtext_editor_scroll_to_line.doc: Scrolls so that a line is visible.

Rtext_editor_set_read_only.doc: A read-only editor can still be scrolled, selected and copied.

Rtext_editor_set_word_wrap.doc: Long lines continue on the next row instead of scrolling sideways. Off by default.

Rtext_editor_set_line_numbers.doc: Shows the line numbers in a margin. Off by default.

Rtext_editor_set_tab_size.doc: Width of a tab, in spaces (4 by default).

Rtext_editor_set_tab_inserts_spaces.doc: R_TRUE makes the Tab key insert spaces instead of a tab character. Off by default.

Rtext_editor_set_syntax.doc: The same as Rtext_editor_set_language with "XML", "C" or NULL.

Rtext_editor_set_font.doc:
R_INVALID_ID uses the font of the theme (or the fixed-width
font, with a language).
0 uses the font size of the theme.

Rtext_editor_set_placeholder.doc: Text shown, dimmed, while the editor is empty.

Rtext_editor_set_zoom.doc:
Zoom of the text: a factor of its font size, 1 = 100 % (0.5 .. 4).
The user zooms with Ctrl + wheel (around the pointer), Ctrl + '+',
Ctrl + '-' and Ctrl + 0 (back to 100 %), keypad included. Set by the
program, the top of the view stays and the zoom callback is not called.
XML: Zoom="1.25".

Rtext_editor_set_zoomable.doc: R_FALSE: Ctrl + wheel and the keys do not zoom (the wheel scrolls). On by default. XML: Zoomable="false".

Rlanguage_get.doc: Reads the description of a language. The strings belong to the library. Returns R_FALSE when it is unknown.

Rlanguage_for_file.doc: Returns The name of the language of a file, from its extension, or NULL.

Rtext_editor_set_language.doc:
Gives the editor a language, by name ("C++", "Python"...), by
another usual name ("cpp", "js") or by the extension of its files
("rs"). NULL or "" removes it. An editor with a language uses the
fixed-width font unless it was given a font.

Rtext_editor_get_language.doc: Returns The name of the language of the editor, or "".

Rtext_editor_set_markdown.doc:
R_TRUE makes the editor an editor of Markdown (the "Markdown"
language; Markdown="true" in XML): the text stays as it is written,
and what it formats shows while typing, strong text in bold,
emphasized text in italic, titles in bold, code, links and marks in
their colors. A label with Rlabel_set_markdown shows the same text
formatted. R_FALSE removes the language.

Rtext_editor_get_token.doc:
What the language of the editor makes of the character at a
position: the colors come from it. R_TOKEN_TEXT without a language.

Rtext_editor_set_completion.doc: R_FALSE stops the editor from proposing words by itself; Ctrl+Space still does. On by default.

Rtext_editor_show_completions.doc: Proposes words for what is before the cursor, as Ctrl+Space does.

Rtext_editor_add_completion.doc:
Called each time the editor gathers its proposals, with the
start of the word being typed: add your own with
Rtext_editor_add_completion (the fields of a structure, the answers of
a language server...). They are listed before the others.
/
typedef void (*RCompletionCallback)(Rid editor, const char* prefix, void* user_data);
RAVEN_API void Rtext_editor_set_completion_callback(Rid editor, RCompletionCallback callback, void* user_data);
/**
Adds a proposal. Only from a completion callback. Proposals that
do not start with the prefix are left out; the others keep the order
they were added in.
A few words shown beside it ("function", "int"), or NULL.

Rtext_editor_add_completion_insert.doc:
Adds a proposal that writes another text than the one it shows
and is matched on: "Threshold", listed and filtered as such, that
writes "Threshold(" when chosen. Only from a completion callback.
What replaces the word being typed; NULL or "" is `text`.

Rtext_editor_set_completion_words.doc:
R_FALSE leaves the words of the language and the names of the
text out of the proposals: only the completion callback's are listed
(a language server that knows better). On by default.

Rtext_editor_set_auto_pairs.doc:
R_FALSE stops the editor from closing brackets and quotes and
from indenting after them. On by default; it only acts with a language.

Rtext_editor_add_marker.doc:
Underlines a part of a line and attaches a message to it, shown
when the pointer rests there: an error of a compiler, a warning.
Markers follow their line when text is added or removed above it, and
go away when their own line is edited.
-1 for the end of the line.

Rtheme_clear_token_colors.doc: Back to the colors Raven picks.

Rheader_bar_set_title.doc: NULL shows the title of the window.

Rheader_bar_set_buttons.doc: Bitmask of RHeaderButtons. All by default; the maximize button only shows on a resizable window.

Rheader_bar_set_button_side.doc:
R_HALIGN_RIGHT: minimize, maximize, close, as on Windows.
R_HALIGN_LEFT: three round colored buttons, as on macOS. Until it is
set, the side is the one of the system the program runs on (left on
macOS, right elsewhere), whatever the look.

Rheader_bar_set_title_notch.doc:
R_TRUE: the title sits in a dark tab hanging from the top edge of
the bar (slanted sides, round bottom corners). XML: TitleStyle="Notch".

Rheader_bar_set_background.doc:
R_FALSE removes the background of the bar: for a header that
floats above the content (in an Overlay) or sits inside a glass panel.

Rdock_area_add_panel.doc:
Adds a panel. The dock area takes ownership of the widget.
Text of its tab.
Where it goes.
A panel of the area to split or to share tabs with, or
R_INVALID_ID for the whole area (with R_DOCK_TAB: the
first group of tabs).
Part of the split space given to the new panel, 0..1
(0 = a half, or a quarter along the whole area).

Rdock_area_move_panel.doc: Moves a panel of the area somewhere else in it.

Rdock_area_close_panel.doc: Removes a panel and deletes it.

Rdock_area_set_panel_icon.doc:
Icon drawn before the title of the tab of a panel (and on the chip while it is dragged).
Texture of the icon, R_INVALID_ID removes it.
Region of the texture (0, 0, 1, 1 : all of it).
R_TRUE: the texture is a mask drawn in the text color of the tab (monochrome icons).

Rdock_area_set_panel_closable.doc: R_FALSE removes the close button of the tab of a panel. Panels can be closed by default.

Rdock_area_hide_panel.doc:
Takes a panel out of the arrangement without deleting it (a
window of an application closed from its menu). Its tab disappears
and its neighbours take its place; the area remembers where it was.

Rdock_area_open_panel.doc: Puts a hidden panel back where it was, and brings its tab to the front (also for a panel that is not hidden).

Rdock_area_is_panel_open.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the panel is in the arrangement (not hidden), shown or behind another tab.

Rdock_area_set_close_hides.doc:
R_TRUE: the close button of a tab hides its panel
(Rdock_area_hide_panel) instead of deleting it. XML: CloseHides="true".
The close callback is asked first either way.

Rdock_area_show_panel.doc: Brings the tab of a panel to the front.

Rdock_area_is_panel_shown.doc: Returns R_TRUE when the panel is the one shown in its group of tabs.

Rdock_area_set_movable.doc: R_FALSE stops the user from moving the panels (the borders can still be dragged).

Rdock_area_save_layout.doc:
Describes how the panels are arranged, as a short text to keep
in a settings file. Panels are named by their widget name
(Rwidget_set_name): unnamed panels are not part of the description.
Returns A string valid until the next call.

Rdock_area_load_layout.doc:
Arranges the panels as a saved description says. Panels of the
area that the description does not name keep a place; names it has
that match no panel are ignored in legacy descriptions. Versioned
descriptions with floating cards reject unknown or duplicate names.
Returns R_FALSE when the text is not a layout (nothing is changed).

Rdock_area_set_tearable.doc:
Called when the user closes a panel, before it is deleted.
Return R_FALSE to keep the panel.
/
typedef int (*RDockCloseCallback)(Rid area, Rid panel, void* user_data);
RAVEN_API void Rdock_area_set_close_callback(Rid area, RDockCloseCallback callback, void* user_data);

/**
Tearing: a tab dragged out of the area takes its panel to a
window of its own (a floating area of the same family), and a tab
dragged from such a window over the area docks it back where it is
dropped. A double click on the tab of a floating window, or closing
that window, puts its panels back where they were. Dragging the only
tab of a floating window moves the window. R_TRUE by default; XML:
Tearable="false". The functions of this area that take a panel also
work on its panels that are in floating windows.

Rdock_area_set_float_mode.doc: Default for future floats/tears; existing floating panels keep their mode.

Rdock_area_float_panel.doc: Floats a panel. Native mode: screen x/y; in-window mode: window-local logical x/y. Returns its containing window.

Rdock_area_dock_panel.doc: A floating panel goes back where it was in the area.

Rdock_area_get_panel_window.doc: The window a floating panel is in, R_INVALID_ID when it is docked in the area.

Risland_set_expanded.doc: Unfolds or folds the island. The changed callback is not called.

Risland_expand_for.doc:
Unfolds the island, and folds it back by itself after a while:
to tell something to the user. It stays open while the pointer is on it.

Risland_set_expand_on_hover.doc: R_TRUE (default): the island unfolds under the pointer and folds back when it leaves.

Risland_set_expand_on_click.doc: R_TRUE (default): a click on the island unfolds or folds it.

Risland_set_attached.doc:
R_TRUE gives the island square upper corners: a notch that hangs
from the edge it touches, instead of a capsule that floats under it.

Risland_set_notch.doc:
R_TRUE: on a screen with a camera housing at its top (the notch
of a MacBook), the island of a window (Rwindow_set_island) lives in the
housing itself, in a window of its own anchored to the screen: it stays
there when the window is moved, and takes the mouse and the keyboard as
usual. Folded, it is the housing grown into two ears: the first Spacer
of its folded content becomes the room of the camera (what is before
it shows on the left, what is after on the right). Unfolded, its
content starts under the camera.

It is in the housing while its window is the last one of the
application the user worked in, is shown, and is on that screen; it
goes back into its window otherwise, and on the window systems and
screens without a housing (where nothing changes). XML: Notch="true".

Risland_is_in_notch.doc: R_TRUE while the island is in the camera housing of the screen.

Rwindow_set_taskbar_progress.doc:
A progress bar on the icon of the application: on the button of
the window in the taskbar (Windows), on the icon in the Dock (macOS),
on the launcher (Linux). There is one icon for the whole application in
the Dock and the launchers: the last window that set it is shown.
From 0 to 1 (not used by NONE and INDETERMINATE).
Returns R_FALSE where the system shows no progress.

Rwindow_request_attention.doc:
Asks the user to look at the window when it is not the active
one: its taskbar button flashes (Windows), the icon bounces in the
Dock (macOS), the window is marked urgent (X11, the launchers of
Linux). `critical`: until the user comes to the window; otherwise a few
times. Nothing happens when the window is already the active one.

Rtaskbar_set_badge.doc:
A short text on the icon of the application: a number of unread
messages, "!". macOS: the badge of the Dock. Windows: a small round
icon on the taskbar buttons of the windows, drawn from the text (one
to three characters fit). Linux: a number only (the text is read as
one; anything else shows nothing). NULL or "": no badge.

Rtaskbar_set_menu.doc:
The menu of the icon of the application in the Dock (macOS),
above the entries of the system. A MENU without a parent: its
MenuItems fire as when chosen in a window (clicked callback, action),
and what changes in it shows the next time the menu opens.
R_INVALID_ID: none. R_FALSE where the system has no such menu.

Rtaskbar_set_jump_list.doc:
The tasks of the jump list of Windows (right click on the button
of the application in the taskbar, or on its tile in the Start menu).
Choosing one starts the application again with its arguments: the
application reads them as any other command line. count 0: none.
R_FALSE where there is no jump list.

Rtray_is_supported.doc:
Returns R_TRUE when the system shows tray icons: always on Windows and
macOS; on Linux, when a host of StatusNotifierItem runs (the panel of
the desktop). An icon made where none runs yet appears when one starts.

Rtray_create.doc:
Puts an icon of the application beside the clock. While one
exists, the application goes on running when its last window closes
(Ris_running): Rquit (or the action app.quit) ends it.
Returns R_INVALID_ID where the system has none.

Rtray_set_icon.doc:
The picture, from tightly packed RGBA8 pixels (straight alpha);
the system scales it (16 to 32 pixels square fit everywhere). Copied.

Rtray_set_tooltip.doc: The text shown when the pointer rests on the icon (and its title for the Linux panels).

Rtray_set_menu.doc:
The menu the system shows for the icon: on a right click
(Windows, Linux), on a click (macOS). A MENU without a parent, whose
MenuItems fire as when chosen in a window; what changes in it shows
the next time it opens. R_INVALID_ID: none.

Rtray_set_clicked_callback.doc:
Called on a click: the left button (activate), the right one
when there is no menu, the middle one. On macOS an icon with a menu
opens it instead.

Rtray_set_title.doc:
A short text shown beside the icon (macOS menu bar), drawn by the
system in its own font and colors; the item widens to fit it. NULL or
"": the icon alone. Systems that show no text there ignore it (the
tooltip is the place for it).

Rtray_get_rect.doc:
Where the icon is on the screen, in the units and coordinates of
Rwindow_set_position (a window can then open just under it).
Returns R_FALSE when the system does not tell (the outputs are then 0).

Rcolor_picker_create.doc:
Raven
raven_tools.h : the widgets of creative tools.

R_WIDGET_COLOR_PICKER   chooses a color
R_WIDGET_TIMELINE       tracks of clips and keys along a time ruler (a sequencer)
R_WIDGET_NODE_GRAPH     nodes linked by wires
R_WIDGET_BLOCK_EDITOR   blocks that snap into each other (Scratch)

Each of them holds a small model (a color; tracks, clips and keys; nodes,
pins and links) that the application fills and reads through the
functions below, or writes in XML. The things inside a timeline or a
graph are named by integers that are only meaningful for that widget, 0
meaning "none"; they are never reused while the widget lives.
/

#ifndef RAVEN_TOOLS_H
#define RAVEN_TOOLS_H

#include "raven_widget.h"


#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* ============================================================================
COLOR PICKER

A square of saturation and value, a strip of hues, a strip of opacity
over a checkerboard, the color before and the color now side by side,
its hexadecimal code, its numbers (red green blue, or hue saturation
value), and a row of swatches. Everything is linked: dragging in the
square moves the numbers, typing a code moves the square.

<ColorPicker Name="tint" Color="#3B82F6" Alpha="true" OnChanged="tint.changed"/>

With Popup="true" the widget is a swatch the size of a button, which
opens the picker in a popup when clicked.
============================================================================

Rcolor_picker_set_color.doc: Sets the color (0..1 each). The callback is not called.

Rcolor_picker_set_hsv.doc:
The same color as hue (0..360), saturation and value (0..1).
The picker remembers the hue of a gray and the saturation of black,
which red, green and blue cannot tell.

Rcolor_picker_set_hex.doc:
Sets the color from text: "#RGB", "#RRGGBB", "#RRGGBBAA" (the
'#' may be left out) or one of the color names of the XML attributes.
A code without opacity leaves the opacity as it is.
Returns R_FALSE when the text is not a color (the color is unchanged).

Rcolor_picker_get_hex.doc: Returns "#RRGGBB", or "#RRGGBBAA" when the opacity is shown and not full. Valid until the color changes.

Rcolor_picker_set_alpha_enabled.doc: R_TRUE (default) shows the opacity strip and the fourth number. R_FALSE: colors are opaque.

Rcolor_picker_set_previous_color.doc:
The color shown next to the current one, to compare with what
was there before: clicking it comes back to it. Rcolor_picker_set_color
does not change it; a popup picker takes it when it opens.

Rcolor_picker_add_swatch.doc: Adds a color to the row of swatches: one click takes it.

Rcolor_picker_set_popup.doc: R_TRUE turns the widget into a swatch that opens the picker in a popup.

Rcolor_picker_set_compact.doc: R_TRUE hides the code and the numbers: only the square, the strips and the swatches.

Rtimeline_set_time.doc: Moves the playhead. The time callback is not called.

Rtimeline_set_snapping.doc: R_FALSE lets items be placed anywhere (holding Alt while dragging does it for one move).

Rtimeline_set_view.doc: The part of the sequence that is shown. Zooming is showing less.

Rtimeline_set_playing.doc:
Makes the playhead run by itself, at the speed of the clock,
calling the time callback at each frame; at the end it stops, or
starts again with Rtimeline_set_loop.

Rtimeline_set_header_width.doc: Width of the column of the names of the tracks. 0 (default): fits the longest name.

Rtimeline_get_header_width.doc: Returns The width of the column of the names, as laid out now.

Rtimeline_set_ruler_height.doc: Height of the ruler of time (and of the markers' flags band). 0 (default): automatic.

Rtimeline_set_default_track_height.doc: Height of the tracks that have none of their own (Rtimeline_set_track_height). 0 (default): automatic.

Rtimeline_add_track.doc: Returns The track, or 0. Tracks are shown in the order they were added.

Rtimeline_remove_track.doc: Removes a track and everything on it.

Rtimeline_get_track.doc: Returns The index-th track from the top, or 0.

Rtimeline_set_track_color.doc: Color of the clips and keys of the track that have none of their own.

Rtimeline_set_track_height.doc: Height of the track in logical units; 0 = the default.

Rtimeline_set_track_locked.doc: A locked track shows its items but does not let the user change them.

Rtimeline_set_track_muted.doc: A muted track is drawn dimmed; what muting means is up to the application.

Rtimeline_set_track_style.doc:
A property of the look of a track: "ClipStyle" (Solid,
Gradient, Tint, Outline), "KeyShape" (Diamond, Circle, Square...),
"KeySize", "ClipRadius", "Background" (its lane), or a part and a
property ("Clip.Glow", "Key.BorderColor"). "" or "Default" gives back
the one of the timeline.
Returns R_FALSE when the name or the value is not one.

Rtimeline_add_clip.doc: Returns The clip, or 0 when the track does not exist.

Rtimeline_add_marker.doc: A named moment of the whole sequence, shown on the ruler and across the tracks.

Rtimeline_clear.doc: Removes every track, clip, key and marker.

Rtimeline_get_item_track.doc: Returns The track of a clip or of a key; 0 for a marker.

Rtimeline_get_item_length.doc: Returns The length of a clip; 0 for a key or a marker.

Rtimeline_set_item.doc: Moves an item: to another track (0 = keep), another start, another length (clips; negative = keep).

Rtimeline_set_item_style.doc:
A property of the look of one clip, key or marker: "Style"
(Solid, Gradient, Tint, Outline: clips), "Shape" (keys), or any
property of its part ("Background", "BorderColor", "Glow",
"CornerRadius", "Foreground" for its label...).

Rtimeline_set_preset.doc: The look the timeline starts from (R_PRESET_AUTO by default; Preset="..." in XML).

Rtimeline_get_item.doc: Returns The index-th item, in the order they were added, or 0.

Rtimeline_select.doc: Selects an item, alone or (add) with the ones already selected.

Rtimeline_set_selection_callback.doc: Called when the selection changed; `item` is the item just clicked, or 0.

Rtimeline_set_activated_callback.doc: Called when an item is double-clicked.

Rtimeline_set_removed_callback.doc:
Called when the user deletes an item (the Delete key), before
it is removed: its values can still be read. Without this callback the
Delete key does nothing: the application decides what can be deleted.

Rnode_graph_add_node.doc: Top-left corner of the node, in the units of the canvas.

Rnode_graph_remove_node.doc: Removes a node, its pins, their links, and the widget it holds.

Rnode_graph_get_node_size.doc: Size of a node on the canvas: Raven works it out from its title, its pins and its content.

Rnode_graph_set_node_color.doc: Color of the header of the node; without one it takes the accent color of the theme.

Rnode_graph_set_node_style.doc:
A property of the look of one node: "HeaderStyle" (Solid,
Gradient, Stripe, Tint, None), "HeaderColor", "TitleColor",
"Background", "BorderColor", "BorderWidth", "CornerRadius", "Glow",
"Icon" (an image file shown before its title), or a part and a property
("Header.Gradient", "Node.ShadowSize"). "" or "Default" gives back the
one of the graph.
Returns R_FALSE when the name or the value is not one.

Rnode_graph_set_node_content.doc:
Puts a widget inside the node, under its pins: the graph owns
it from now on. R_INVALID_ID removes (and deletes) the one it had.

Rnode_graph_set_node_name.doc:
Name of the node, the `Name` of its XML element: what
<Link From="name.pin"> and Rnode_graph_find_node look for. Not shown.

Rnode_graph_find_node.doc: Returns The node of that name, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_node_user_data.doc: Value the application attaches to a node.

Rnode_graph_add_input.doc: Free text, or NULL for a pin that links to any type. return The pin, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_name.doc: Name of the pin for Rnode_graph_find_pin and for the links of XML; a pin without one answers to its label.

Rnode_graph_find_pin.doc: Returns The pin of a node with that name (or label), or 0.

Rnode_graph_get_pin_position.doc: Where a pin is on the canvas (the middle of its dot).

Rnode_graph_get_input.doc: Returns The index-th input (or output) of a node, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_type_color.doc: Color of the pins of a type and of the links between them.

Rnode_graph_set_type_style.doc:
A property of the pins of a type and of their links: "Shape"
(Circle, Ring, Square, Diamond, Triangle, Arrow), "Size", "Glow",
"LinkShape" (Bezier, Straight, Step, Angled), "LinkWidth", "LinkGlow".

Rnode_graph_connect.doc:
Links an output to an input, as the user does by dragging.
The connect callback is not asked.
Returns The link; 0 when the pins cannot be linked (two inputs, the
same node, different types).

Rnode_graph_get_input_link.doc: Returns The link that arrives at an input pin, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_view.doc: What the middle of the widget shows: a point of the canvas, and how large (1 = one unit per logical unit).

Rnode_graph_to_canvas.doc: Converts a point of the widget (from its corner, as in the events) to the canvas, and back, with the view as it is shown now.

Rnode_graph_frame_all.doc: Moves and zooms so that every node shows.

Rnode_graph_set_grid_visible.doc: R_FALSE hides the grid of dots (shown by default).

Rnode_graph_set_flow_visible.doc:
The pulses of light that run along the links, from output to
input. By default they run while the pointer is over the graph, and
the window rests the rest of the time. R_TRUE makes them run all the
time (the window then draws without pause); R_FALSE stops them.

Rnode_graph_set_read_only.doc: R_TRUE: the user can look but not move, link or delete.

Rnode_graph_set_preset.doc: The look the graph starts from (R_PRESET_AUTO by default; Preset="..." in XML).

Rnode_graph_set_moved_callback.doc: Called for each node the user moved, when the button is released.

Rnode_graph_set_selection_callback.doc: Called when the selection changed; `item` is the node just clicked, or 0.

Rnode_graph_set_removed_callback.doc:
Called when the user deletes a node (the Delete key), before
it is removed. Without this callback the Delete key only removes
links: the application decides whether nodes can be deleted.

Rnode_graph_set_activated_callback.doc: Called when the user double-clicks a node (to open what it stands for).

Rnode_graph_set_wire_dropped_callback.doc:
A wire the user pulled from a pin was released on nothing: `item` is
that pin, x, y where it was dropped (to offer a node to connect it to). The
wire draws back as usual.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_clicked_callback.doc:
A pin was clicked, not dragged (`item` is the pin, x, y on the canvas):
the application may link in two clicks (Rnode_graph_set_pin_emphasis shows where
the second may go). With this callback such a click neither detaches the wire
of an input nor counts as a wire dropped on nothing.

Rnode_graph_get_node_at.doc: The node under a point of the widget (x, y as in the events: Rnode_graph_to_canvas), or 0.

Rnode_graph_get_pin_at.doc: The pin near a point of the widget (or whose tag is under it: Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag), or 0 (a menu for a pin).

Rnode_graph_set_link_hidden.doc:
R_TRUE: the link stays (its pins are linked, the application keeps
it) but is not drawn and not picked: its two ends are shown otherwise (pin
tags naming it, as the labels of a schematic stand for a wire).

Rnode_graph_set_pin_emphasis.doc:

Rnode_graph_get_tag_at.doc: The pin whose tag (Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag) is under a point of the widget, or 0: the chip only, not the pin.

Rnode_graph_set_pin_tag_lit.doc:

Rnode_graph_set_pin_label_width.doc:

Rnode_graph_set_node_badge_color.doc: Color of the badge pill of one node (Rnode_graph_set_node_badge); its text turns dark or light to suit it. A negative component restores the look's color.

Rlocale_load_csv.doc:
Raven
raven_locale.h : translations and the conventions of a language.

Translations live in CSV tables: one row per text, one column per language.
The first row names the columns: "key", then a language code per column
(the codes are free: "en", "fr", "pt-BR", "ar"...).

key,en,fr,ar
menu.file,File,Fichier,ملف
greeting,"Hello, {0}!","Bonjour, {0} !",مرحبا {0}
files.one,{n} file,{n} fichier,ملف واحد
files.other,{n} files,{n} fichiers,{n} ملفات

The usual CSV rules apply: fields with commas, quotes or line breaks are
quoted, "" inside quotes is one quote. Lines starting with # are comments.
A UTF-8 BOM is accepted. Several tables can be loaded: they add up, and a
key loaded again replaces the old text. A table loaded from a file is read
again when the file is saved, while live reload is on (Rxml_set_live_reload).

In C:
Rlocale_load_csv("strings.csv");
Rlocale_set_language(Rlocale_get_system_language());
Rlabel_set_text(label, Rtr("menu.file"));

In XML, an attribute that starts with @ is a key: the widget shows its
translation and follows the language when it changes ("@@" for a text that
really starts with @):
<Button Text="menu.file" Tooltip="menu.file.tip"/>
and a document can load its tables itself:
<Strings Source="strings.csv"/>

A key with no translation in the language shows the text of the fallback
language (the first column, or Rlocale_set_fallback_language), then the key.

The functions are for the UI thread. The strings they return stay valid
until the tables or the language change (Rtr), or for the next 16 calls
(Rtr_format, Rtr_plural, Rlocale_format_number).
/

#ifndef RAVEN_LOCALE_H
#define RAVEN_LOCALE_H

#include "raven_core.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* ---- tables ---- */

/** brief Loads a CSV table of translations from a file. Returns the number of keys read, -1 on an error.

Rlocale_set_text.doc: Adds or replaces one text of one language.

Rlocale_get_language_count.doc: Number of languages in the tables, and their codes, in the order of the columns.

Rlocale_set_language.doc:
Chooses the language: an exact code ("pt-BR"), or its first part
("pt") when the tables have no such column. Every widget that shows a key
is updated, and the layout of the windows follows its direction (an
Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu language is laid out from right to left,
see Rset_layout_direction). Returns R_FALSE when no column matches (the
language is set all the same: the texts fall back).

Rlocale_get_system_language.doc: The language of the user, from the system ("fr-FR", "en-US"...).

Rlocale_set_fallback_language.doc: The language whose texts are shown when the current one has none (default: the first column).

Rlocale_is_rtl.doc: R_TRUE when the language is written from right to left.

Rlocale_set_changed_callback.doc: Called after the language or the tables changed (the widgets are already updated).

Rtr.doc: The text of a key in the current language (see the fallbacks above). Never NULL.

Rtr_exists.doc: R_TRUE when the key has a text in the current language or the fallback one.

Rtr_format.doc:
The text of a key with its {0} {1} ... replaced by the arguments
(translators may put them in any order). "{{" is a brace.

Rtr_plural.doc:
The plural form of a key for a count: the key followed by the CLDR
category of the count in the current language (".zero", ".one", ".two",
".few", ".many", ".other"), else ".other", else the key itself. {n} is
replaced by the count, written in the conventions of the language.

Rwidget_set_text_key.doc:
Makes a widget show a key: an attribute ("Text", "Tooltip",
"Title", "Placeholder"... any attribute that takes a text) is set to the
translation now and every time the language changes. NULL or "" stops it.
Same as Rwidget_set_attribute(widget, attribute, "key").

Rlocale_format_number.doc: A number written in the conventions of the language: decimal separator and digit grouping ("1 234,5" in French).

Raccessibility_set_text_scale.doc:
Raven
raven_accessibility.h : interfaces for everyone.

Screen readers. Every window of Raven is exposed to the screen reader of
the system: UI Automation on Windows (Narrator, NVDA, JAWS), NSAccessibility
on macOS (VoiceOver), AT-SPI on Linux (Orca). Nothing is needed for that:
the widgets say what they are (a button, a check box, a slider, a list and
its items, a tab...), their name (the text they show, or the label just
before them), their value and their state, and they can be used from the
screen reader (press, toggle, set a value, expand). The focus is followed,
and the application can have a message read (Raccessibility_announce).
What a widget cannot know (an icon button, a drawing) is given with
Rwidget_set_accessible_name / _description / _role, or in XML with the
attributes AccessibleName, AccessibleDescription, AccessibleRole and
AccessibleHidden.

Sight. The size of every text (Raccessibility_set_text_scale), themes of
high contrast, a focus that is always shown and thicker, animations that
can be stopped, and color filters for the color blind: a correction that
moves the colors they confuse to colors they tell apart, and simulations
for those who design for them. Raccessibility_follow_system takes the
settings of the system.

Writings. Right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu) are
drawn in their order, with their letters joined, and the layout mirrors
itself for them (raven_layout.h, Rset_layout_direction). The characters
that the fonts of the application do not have (other alphabets, Chinese,
Japanese, Korean, symbols, emoji in color) are taken from the fonts of the
system. See raven_locale.h for translations.
/

#define RAVEN_ACCESSIBILITY_H

#include "raven_core.h"

#endif

/** brief What the screen reader says of the widget; NULL: what it shows (or the label before it).

Rwidget_get_accessible_name.doc: The name the screen reader uses (given, or found). Valid until the next call.

Rwidget_set_accessible_description.doc: A longer explanation, read after the name.

Rwidget_get_accessible_role.doc: The role the screen reader sees (given, or the one of the type).

Rwidget_set_accessible_hidden.doc: R_TRUE: hidden from screen readers, with what it contains (decoration).

Rwidget_set_accessible_labelled_by.doc: The widget is named by another one (a label): its text is the name.

Rwidget_set_accessible_action.doc:
Explicit screen-reader press action, including for custom widgets.
NULL removes the override. Does not change pointer or keyboard handling.
Disabled widgets (including disabled ancestors) cannot be pressed.

Rwidget_set_accessible_checked.doc:
Override the checked state: 1 checked, 0 unchecked, -1 restores the
widget's default (not checkable for a custom widget). The application owns
this state; a press callback updates it when appropriate.

Raccessibility_announce.doc: Has a message read (a save that ended, an error). `assertive`: interrupts what is being read.

Raccessibility_is_screen_reader_active.doc: R_TRUE when a screen reader is reading the windows of the application.

Rvulkan_set_external_device.doc:
Makes Raven use an existing device. Raven does not destroy these objects.
VkInstance
VkPhysicalDevice
VkDevice
VkQueue supporting graphics and presentation
Family index of `queue`

Rvulkan_get_graphics_queue.doc: Opaque VkQueue used for rendering and presentation.

Rvulkan_simulate_device_lost.doc:
Behaves as if the GPU had answered VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, to test
how an application recovers (Rset_device_reset_callback). Raven
recovers at the next frame by making a new device: every handle
returned above changes. Does nothing with an external device
(Rvulkan_set_external_device), whose loss the application handles.

Rvulkan_texture_create_from_image_view.doc:
Wraps an application image so that widgets (Image, Viewport) can show it.
The image must be in VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL whenever Raven
renders, and must outlive the texture. Raven does not destroy it: destroy it
after Rtexture_destroy, which returns once Raven no longer uses the image.

The values of the image are shown as they are (the UI is not color
managed): use a UNORM view of an sRGB-encoded image. Alpha is honored, so
clear the image with alpha 1 unless the viewport should be see-through.

Raw VkImageView handle (cast to uint64_t).
Raw VkSampler handle, or 0 for the Raven linear sampler.

Rvulkan_texture_set_image_view.doc:
Points an existing wrapped texture to another image view (after a resize).
Returns once Raven no longer uses the previous view, which can then be destroyed.

Rvulkan_texture_create_shared.doc:
Creates an RGBA8 texture whose memory can be imported by another
API or process (OpenGL GL_EXT_memory_object, another Vulkan device).
Requires VK_KHR_external_memory_fd (POSIX) or _win32 (Windows).
Returns R_INVALID_ID when the device cannot export memory.

Rvulkan_texture_get_shared_info.doc: Exports the memory of a shared texture. Each call returns a new handle.

Rbackend_device_lost.doc:
Tells Raven that the device of the backend was lost. Thread-safe:
call it from the backend (render thread) when the API reports it. At the
next frame Raven calls Shutdown and Init again, then remakes the
surfaces, the textures and the shaders (see Rset_device_reset_callback).
Until then RenderFrame may simply return.

Rpixels_alloc.doc: Allocates a pixel buffer released by Rpixels_free. Thread-safe.

Rhost_platform_is_active.doc: Returns R_TRUE while the running library uses the host platform.

Rhost_window_set_size.doc: Size of a host window in pixels, and pixels per logical unit.

Rhost_inject_mouse_leave.doc: The pointer left the window: hover states end.

Rhost_inject_key.doc: R_TRUE for a key held down (auto-repeat).

Rhost_inject_focus.doc: The window gained or lost the keyboard. Losing it closes popups and drops captures.

Rhost_inject_close.doc: The user asked to close the window (its close callback decides).
